title: Side setback, walls 3.6 m to 7 m high (R2-R40)
text: C3.4.1 Buildings are set back from lot boundaries in accordance with Table 3.4a. Refer Figure 3.4a, b, c. ii. For R2-R40, the stated setback distances may be reduced by half the width of an adjoining pedestrian access way to a maximum reduction of 2m (refer to Figure 3.4d). Table 3.4a Lot boundary setbacks, side setback: R2 10m; R2.5 7.5m; R5 and above, Wall height 3.6m to 7m: 1.5m.

replaces.note: R2 10 m and R2.5 7.5 m unchanged; R5+ now by wall height only
wall length and major-opening dimensions dropped

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 2 - Single Houses.pdf

notes: R2 and R2.5 have flat side setbacks (10 m, 7.5 m) regardless of wall height. Applies only where the building has walls 3.6 m to 7 m high (condition on building.has_walls_3_6_to_7m); the band does not depend on the building's maximum wall height. Reduction (ii) is limited to a pedestrian access way (ROW, communal street and battleaxe leg credits of Part B dropped, register ch2-057). Rounding gap between bands unresolved. Split from the R50+ rule so the reduction is confined to R2-R40.

verified.note: Table 3.4a prints the bands as 'Wall height up to 3.5m', 'Wall height 3.6m to 7m' and 'Wall height above 7.1m', leaving 3.5-3.6 m and 7.0-7.1 m undefined; Table 2A (p7) prints the top band as '7.1m and above'. The encoded band conditions (> 3.5, > 7.0) are an inference.
